speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg. To understand what is causing this, can you tell me how long the lesion has been present and if it started as a small bump or appeared suddenly?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Crohn's Disease-associated Pyoderma Gangrenosum.

Based on your history of Crohn's disease and the rapid development of a painful ulcer with undermined borders following minor trauma (an ant bite), this presentation is highly characteristic of Pyoderma Gangrenosum, which can be triggered by infection or flare-ups of your underlying condition.
